metadata.topic: Open Source Agent Eval Harness Comparison 2026

landscapeOverview.marketTrend: The open-source agent eval harness space exploded in 2025-2026, moving from simple LLM output scoring to full-system evaluation. Key trends include: (1) trace-based scoring over final-answer checking, (2) multi-dimensional metrics (cost, latency, reliability, safety), (3) CI/CD integration for regression gates, (4) LLM-as-judge with calibration, (5) reproducibility-first methodology with variance decomposition.
keySegments: Lightweight developer tools (agent-eval-harness by Siddharth-1001, evalh)

competitors.name: MASEval
competitors.description: Framework-agnostic library for multi-agent system evaluation. Treats the entire system as the unit of analysis — topology, orchestration, error handling. Supports GAIA, AgentBench benchmarks. Agents from any framework via adapters.
differentiators: Multi-agent native with per-agent tracing
System-level comparison (not just LLM swapping)
Agent-agnostic: AutoGen, LangChain, custom frameworks via adapters
Lifecycle hooks for tracing/logging/metrics
arXiv paper: 2603.08835 (ParameterLab)
Key finding: framework choice matters as much as model choice

competitors.name: ClawBench
competitors.description: A reproducibility-first benchmark that scores the full stack (harness, config, and model) — not just the LLM. Trace-based trajectory scoring, 4-axis evaluation (completion, trajectory, behavior, judge), 13 failure modes, variance decomposition, dynamical-systems diagnostics (trapped/limit-cycle/diffusive regimes).
differentiators: Core v1: 19 signal-curated tasks from 40-task pool (drops 21 noisy tasks)
47% of 40-task variance is seed noise — quantified transparently
Dynamical-systems diagnostics: per-run regime classification
Constraint Index C(q) for principled task weighting
Configuration Diagnostic: fingerprint, predict, explain, recommend
Partner Trace Spec for cross-harness reproducibility
180+ stars, most sophisticated in the space

competitors.name: reaatech/agent-eval-harness
competitors.description: End-to-end agent evaluation for trajectory analysis, tool-use correctness, cost-per-task, latency budgets, regression suites with golden trajectories, LLM-as-judge with calibration. Composable packages across 11 packages.
differentiators: Full TypeScript ecosystem (unique in Python-dominated space)
CI/CD regression gates with JUnit/XML/GitHub Annotations/PR comments
Three-layer MCP tool server (judge, suite, gate)
Golden trajectory creation and curation workflow
Provider-agnostic LLM-as-judge with multi-model consensus
OpenTelemetry tracing and structured logging

competitors.name: PawBench
competitors.description: A benchmark for evaluating LLM x harness performance together. 150 tasks, 9 models, 3 harnesses (QwenPaw, OpenClaw, Hermes). Task slices and diagnostic traces. Part of OpenJudge ecosystem.
differentiators: Co-evaluation: model AND harness scored together
150 tasks from 6 source benchmarks
Harness gaps visible even when model is fixed (up to 11.5-point spread)
QwenPaw (74.9 avg), OpenClaw (72.9), Hermes (69.3) — harness matters
Diagnostic traces for regression attribution

competitors.name: ProofAgent Harness
competitors.description: Domain-aware adversarial evaluation with jury-based scoring. 183 bundled traps across 11 families (GDPR, HIPAA, PCI, SOX, prompt injection, etc.). 3-Harness-Juror Delphi consensus scoring.
differentiators: Multi-turn adversarial campaigns (not single-shot)
3-Harness-Juror Delphi consensus (independent re-vote on disagreement)
183 bundled traps across 11 families
Domain-aware planning + scoring (HIPAA, PCI, malware-gen)
CI-grade evaluation reports with assertions-style thresholds
Positioning: 'pytest for AI agents'

competitors.name: OpenAgentBench
competitors.description: Evaluates agents as stateful control systems, not transcript generators. Scores tool-choice optimality, privilege safety, memory hygiene, RAG faithfulness, recovery behavior, multi-agent coordination.
differentiators: Real environment-state verification (not just output scoring)
Tool-selection optimality scoring
Privilege misuse and escalation checks
Memory contamination benchmarking
Agent Chaos Lab for failure injection
Pareto Frontier Evaluator across quality, cost, and latency

competitors.name: Kensa
competitors.description: Open-source harness for evaluating coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini CLI). Capture-then-generate-then-eval workflow. Auto-instrumentation with OTel, zero code changes.
differentiators: Purpose-built for coding agent evaluation
Capture real agent runs -> synthesize scenarios via LLM
5 built-in skills (audit, generate scenarios, generate judges, validate judge, diagnose errors)
MCP server integration for LLM clients
Zero code changes to agent (auto-instrumentation)
Free, MIT licensed

competitors.name: agent-eval-harness (Siddharth-1001)
competitors.description: Lightweight open-source evaluation harness for agentic AI systems. Supports LangGraph/LangChain, OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI, Anthropic, PydanticAI. 4 metric dimensions: tool success, hallucination, latency, cost.
differentiators: Framework adapters for major agent frameworks
4 automated metric dimensions
Local dashboard for trace visualization
Side-by-side comparison with HTML export
No vendor lock-in, all data stays local
Decorator-based tracing for non-framework code

competitors.name: CUBE Harness
competitors.description: Open-source harness for the CUBE Standard benchmark protocol. Universal evaluation platform with Ray parallel execution. Agent-agnostic, benchmark-agnostic, RL-ready trajectory format.
differentiators: Based on CUBE Standard benchmark protocol (AI Alliance)
Ray integration for parallel episode execution
RL-ready trajectory format with full LLM call logging
Benchmark agnostic: MiniWob, WebArena, OSWorld
Alpha stage — still evolving

competitors.name: evalh
competitors.description: A boring, config-driven harness for evaluating AI systems. One YAML drives the run. 13 built-in evaluators. Supports A/B testing, fleet evals, branch comparison, drift detection.
differentiators: Single YAML configuration drives everything
13 built-in evaluators (text checks, tool assertions, LLM-judge, schema, gates, etc.)
Variants: N x M cases x system configurations for A/B testing
Drift detection: promote baseline, evalh drift surfaces regressions
Offline, backtesting, and online-eval modes
6 adapter families, 5 executor backends, 8 observability integrations

competitors.name: Harness Bench
competitors.description: A workbench for creating, observing, analyzing, and auto-improving agent harnesses. Includes Improvers — automated research loops that analyze failures and propose harness mutations.
differentiators: Full loop: create + observe + analyze + auto-improve
Improvers: automated DSPy-like research loops for entire harness
Natural language trace analysis ('what's causing failures on billing flow?')
vs observability: 'They watch. We watch and then fix.'
vs DSPy: 'It optimizes prompts. We optimize the entire harness.'

keyInsights: Framework choice matters as much as model choice (MASEval); harness gaps produce 10+ point spreads (PawBench)
47% of benchmark variance is seed noise — reproducibility is the #1 unaddressed problem (ClawBench)
The market is fragmenting into focused niches: adversarial/security (ProofAgent), coding agents (Kensa), TypeScript ecosystems (reaatech)
LLM-as-judge is now standard but with guardrails: capped contribution, gated on deterministic checks, multi-model consensus
Trace-based scoring (scoring the process, not just the output) is the defining architectural shift of 2026
CI/CD integration is table stakes — regression gates, JUnit output, PR comments
No single dominant framework has emerged; the space is still in 'Cambrian explosion' phase
Configuration/harness optimization is emerging as a separate concern from model optimization
recommendedAngle: The 2026 open-source agent eval harness landscape is undergoing a 'Cambrian explosion'. Unlike 2024-2025 where the field focused on improving LLM outputs, 2026 tools focus on evaluating the entire agent system — harness, configuration, tooling, and model as a unified stack. The most differentiated angle: reproducible benchmarking that quantifies noise, scores process over output, and treats harness selection as a first-class decision alongside model selection.
